Proposition
[Equivalence of the two surface matrix estimates] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0294, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0295 ↗ def:chow-ii-hamilton-harnack-quadratic ↗ prop:chow-ii-surface-matrix-harnack 1. ch15:15.13\group Surface Harnack Estimates

In dimension two with $R>0$, Hamilton's inequality $Q\ge 0$ is equivalent to \[ abla _i abla _jR+\left( rac{R^2}{2}+ rac{R}{2t} ight)g_{ij} - rac1R abla _iR abla _jR\ge 0, \] and hence to the matrix inequality for $\log R$.
Proof

\sketch Use $R_{ij}=Rg_{ij}/2$ and write every two-form as $U=f\, e^1\wedge e^2$. Completing the square in $f$ gives

\[ 2Q= abla _V abla _VR+\left( rac{R^2}{2}+ rac{R}{2t} ight)|V|^2 - rac{\langle abla R,V angle ^2}{R} + rac{(\langle abla R,V angle -2fR)^2}{R}. \]

Minimizing in $f$, then varying $V$, yields the displayed tensor inequality. Dividing by $R$ is precisely the Hessian identity for $\log R$.

□
